items.title: Bobby Johnson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: As a matter of fact he was one of the ones who taught me how to play and how to act and all that kind of stuff.

ctx.x: Oh yeah. Well that’s true. That’s the reason why I knew so many musicians. During those days, this was during the days of prohibition. And each town, like the high sheriff or whoever, you could get into his pocket, he would allow one speakeasy on a certain side of town. And we had just one. I lived on the east side of Pensacola. But sometimes I don’t particularly care too much about it, but Pensacola I could say that it wasn’t a Jim Crow town, it was like, I lived, to be frank with you, I came up in an exclusive…
